quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: From top to bottom, what is the correct order of colors on a traffic light?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights are ordered with red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.
questions.explanation: Move your vehicle completely off the road if possible. Keep all four wheels away from the traffic lanes.

questions.question: What should you use to see better when driving in rain or fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off the water and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a roundabout?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Decrease your speed.
Maintain your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach a roundabout. Roundabouts are meant to be driven slowly.

questions.question: When turning left from a one-way street with multiple lanes onto a two-way street, which lane should you start in?

options.text: The far left lane.
Any available lane.
The lane closest to the middle of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: The far left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the far left lane of a one-way street.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the immediate left side of the cab.
On the immediate left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the immediate left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Truck blind spots are much larger than car blind spots. The driver cannot see behind the truck or to the immediate left. If you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: What must you do when you have a green arrow?

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn. But first, yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: If there is a single broken white line on the highway, what can you do?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What are "no zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close that they block the truck driver's ability to stop and turn safely.
Areas where cars have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Areas where cars have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close that they block the truck driver's ability to stop and turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely. Being in a "no zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: Which statement is true about taking medications while driving?

options.text: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications are safe for driving if you use the recommended dose.
Any medication prescribed by a doctor is safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medications can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy. Know how your medication affects you before driving.

questions.question: You have been parked with your turn signal on for a long time, and traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Continue waiting and let traffic go first.
Slowly move your vehicle into the traffic lane.
Drive on the shoulder until there is a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue waiting and let traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When you are parked on the side of the road, you must yield to traffic already on the road when you re-enter.

questions.question: You are behind a motorcycle and want to pass. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use all of the lane.
Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder.
Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give a motorcycle a full lane when passing. Never share a lane with a motorcycle. Returning to the original lane too soon can force the rider off the road.

questions.question: On freezing, wet days, where is ice most likely to hide?

options.text: On roads near the tops of hills.
On bridges and overpasses.
On asphalt roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: On bridges and overpasses.
questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before regular roads. Ice can form on them without warning.

questions.question: When do you consent to a chemical test for alcohol in your blood, breath, or urine?

options.text: Only if you have been drinking alcohol.
Whenever you drive in California.
Only if you have been in a collision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever you drive in California.
questions.explanation: By driving in California, you agree to be tested for alcohol or drugs if you are arrested for suspected drunk driving.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection at the speed limit when the light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed through the intersection.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will turn red soon. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, proceed with caution.

questions.question: When entering traffic from a parked position at the curb, what should you do?

options.text: Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large enough gap to reach the speed of other traffic.
Wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large enough gap to reach the speed of other traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough to speed up to match other traffic.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light before proceeding.
Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
Stop before crossing the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be cautious. Watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead on your side has red lights flashing, what must you do?

options.text: Slow to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, it is loading or unloading students. You must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. If you are turning in that direction, prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: A yellow traffic light warns that the light will change to red soon. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Keep going and leave the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going and leave the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, clear the intersection as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep while driving and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep while driving and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes mistakes about speed and distance. It increases crash risk and slows your decision-making. When tired, you might fall asleep at the wheel and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: When entering the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At about the same speed as freeway traffic.
At the posted speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At about the same speed as freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at about the same speed as traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: You can get a speeding ticket for driving 55 mph in a 55 mph zone if:

options.text: You never can, because it is always legal.
Road or weather conditions require a slower speed.
You are only approaching a sharp curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road or weather conditions require a slower speed.
questions.explanation: California has a Basic Speed Law. You cannot drive faster than is safe for current conditions, even if you are below the speed limit. Consider other vehicles, road surface condition, bicyclists and pedestrians, and weather when choosing your speed.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you should:

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road is coming up ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road is coming up ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to situations that may not be obvious. This sign warns that a side road intersects ahead.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane if you:

options.text: Cannot see the vehicle on your right side.
See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
Have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane after passing, make sure you have enough space. When you see both of the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to return safely.

questions.question: When driving in heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Fog lights may help if your vehicle has them.

questions.question: Which vehicles must always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Tank trucks marked with hazardous materials labels.
Motor homes or pickup trucks towing a boat trailer.
Any vehicle with three or more axles weighing over 4,000 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tank trucks marked with hazardous materials labels.
questions.explanation: Trucks carrying hazardous materials must stop before crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: What usually causes a locked wheel skid?

options.text: Braking too hard at a slow speed
Braking lightly at a slow speed
Braking too hard at a fast speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking too hard at a fast speed
questions.explanation: A locked wheel skid is usually caused by braking too hard while driving at high speed. Use brakes smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: When a blind person using a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street, you should:

options.text: Always let them cross first.
Tell them where to cross the street.
Only let them cross first at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always let them cross first.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind people may use a guide dog or carry a white cane. Always yield the right-of-way to a person using a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: When driving behind a large truck on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Follow closer than you would a passenger car.
Follow farther back than you would a passenger car.
Drive to the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow farther back than you would a passenger car.
questions.explanation: Stay farther back from large trucks than passenger vehicles because trucks have large blind spots.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming car has bright headlights on, making it hard to see the road. You should:

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the oncoming car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the driver will give you space to return to your lane.
Assume the driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the driver will give you space to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even with a signal, do not assume the space you want is free or that other drivers will let you pass.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Watch for people crossing.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This orange warning sign tells drivers that roadwork is coming. Stay alert for temporary traffic control devices in work zones.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to return to the right lane when:

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you cannot see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Do not return to your original lane until you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: You may pass a vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means drivers may cross to change lanes. A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line only. Only change lanes when it is safe.
